title: Two-dimensional weak-interface supershear refinement contract
purpose: Require preservation of the supershear mechanism, energy closure, and convergence of one representative fixed-distance front speed under proportional in-plane mesh refinement and explicit time-step refinement.
physics: near-incompressible finite-strain plane-stress Neo-Hookean strip with ten or more cells through the height, homogeneous preload, smooth remote impact, a fixed bilinear Mode-I cohesive interface, and a precrack

execution.evidence: The opt-in public benchmark compares a 30x10 baseline, near-proportional 40x14 and 60x20 spatial refinements, and a 30x10 run with the stable time increment halved. It is kept outside per-commit CI because the complete local run is intentionally expensive.

observables: Resolved supershear classification and fitted speed normalized by the prestrained reference-coordinate shear speed.
Interface and transverse cell counts, stable time increment, simultaneous failure fraction, and rapid distributed-failure fraction.
A local 0.3-length speed window for peak-speed mechanism classification and one fixed x=[0.8,1.8] propagation interval for refinement convergence.
Complete bulk, kinetic, cohesive, prescribed-work, and energy-balance ledger at retained frames.
Least-squares fit quality and successive relative representative-speed changes under proportional spatial refinement and time-step halving.
Separate mechanism_preserved and speed_converged decisions so a robust regime classification cannot be mistaken for an asymptotically converged crack speed.
acceptance: All four runs remain supershear with fewer than ten percent of intact facets failing in one increment.
Every run closes the complete energy ledger within 0.5 percent.
Every representative fixed-distance fit must have R-squared of at least 0.95.
Each successive spatial representative-speed change must remain below ten percent.
Halving the 30x10 time increment must change representative speed by less than two percent.
limitations: The four cases preserve resolved supershear, close the energy ledger, and pass the declared representative-speed refinement gates.
The accepted result is a two-dimensional numerical mechanism and observation contract, not a publication-parameter fit or curve-level reproduction.
The local plane-stress membrane still requires a thin-three-dimensional cross-check and an independent near-incompressibility study.
The V4 interface is normally preloaded and therefore cannot use the traction-free principal surface-wave oracle as a prestrained Rayleigh boundary.
